title: Field fibre of single locally free cohomology
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $P$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-derived-category] whose terms are finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $d,i,r\in\mathbb N$. Assume $P^n=0$ for $n<0$ and $n>d$, $H^q(P)=0$ for all $q\in\mathbb N$ other than $i$, and $H^i(P)$ finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. For every field $R$ and morphism $f:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$, the termwise pullback $f^*P$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is homotopy equivalent to the single complex on $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}^r$ in degree $i$. A homotopy equivalence consists of chain maps in both directions whose composites are chain homotopic to the identity.

proof.text: Strictly nonnegative support makes the negative cohomology zero. Together with the given nonnegative vanishing this leaves exactly H^i(P). The standard truncation maps identify P in the derived category with H^i(P) in degree i. Since H^i(P) is locally free it is flat. Compute derived pullback on both bounded flat complexes termwise: the fibre is a single ordinary fibre of H^i(P), of rank r.

Sheaves of modules on Spec R for a field R are equivalent to R-vector spaces, by moduleSpecΓFunctor. In each degree split the inclusion of boundaries into cycles and cycles into the term by choosing vector-space complements. The differential gives an isomorphism from each complement of cycles to the next boundaries. Its inverse defines the contraction on these two-term summands. The remaining summands are the cohomology vector spaces; only degree i remains, and a basis identifies it with R^r. Transport the resulting homotopy equivalence back to module sheaves.
